key_insight: Differentiable inverse rendering estimates per-pixel optical attenuation from a single OCT image by optimizing through a physics-based image-formation model.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support quantitative tissue characterization in intravascular OCT, but clinical diagnostic benefit remains unestablished.
method: Use a differentiable physics-based forward model of OCT image formation.
Recover per-pixel attenuation through gradient descent without training data or segmentations.
Keep the optimization procedure unchanged when replacing the forward model or target optical parameter.
evidence_signal: The method was checked against analytical solutions, validated on five in vitro phantoms, and applied without modification to 29,269 clinical intravascular OCT images from 128 patients.
watch_item: Clinical application does not establish tissue-level accuracy; performance may depend on how well the forward model captures real imaging conditions.
paper_title: Differentiable Inverse Rendering Recovers Intrinsic Properties from Intravascular Optical Coherence Tomography
